brief: The diorama has been clickable since before this loop began, and nothing on screen says so. cv's click handler unprojects to a cell and gives six different real responses — a bed takes a scattered handful of a named species, the lawn takes a daisy, the pond takes crumbs and the ducks arrive like a small navy, the fountain takes a coin, the river takes a pebble, the lane takes crumbs and birds land — each with its own written ticker line. The controls strip offers Pause and Speed and no hint that the picture itself answers. A viewer looking at this for thirty seconds will never find any of it, which makes an undiscovered feature the single largest gap between what the town is and what it appears to be. Make the touch discoverable without spoiling it: the cursor should tell you that the cell under the pointer will answer, and a first-time viewer should be invited exactly once. Whatever you add has to be quiet enough to live in a piece that is mostly meant to be watched.
seams: GRASS / BED / CBED / WATER / SIDE / ROAD
successLooksLike: Somebody who has never seen the piece discovers they can touch it inside the first thirty seconds, and a screenshot of the idle diorama is no busier than it is today.
avoid: Do not add new click responses — there are six and this brief is about making them findable, not about having more. No tutorial overlay, no modal, no persistent on-canvas text. Do not let the invitation repeat: one, and it does not come back. Watch the ticker queue's drop policy (TICK_DWELL 2.5 s, cap 2, 6 s staleness) — an invitation that competes with a bell strike will lose, and it should lose gracefully rather than be shown late.
